segments.t: Kostya volunteers to bring the champagne to room 202 himself so he can film Louis and Polina together as proof for Nastya. Meanwhile, Senya and Fedya finish feeding their model for the third time and eagerly await their promised reward.
Давай я сам принесу вам шампанское.
Принесёшь прямо в номер, это отлично!
Запомни, у нас двести второй номер.
Большое спасибо тебе за помощь, Костя.
Саша, присмотри пока за моим баром.
Только смотри не делай как Луи!
Скажи, тебе было сегодня очень вкусно?
Молодцы, вы честно заслужили свою награду.
Ну давай уже скорее награждай нас!
Мы честно кормили тебя два дня.

Мы уже закрыли глаза и ждём.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Давай я сам принесу вам шампанское.
'Let me bring you the champagne myself.' Kostya makes this update on cue: starting with "davay" is the classic everyday Russian way to say "come on, let's do this" between people on close terms.
Принесёшь прямо в номер, это отлично!
'You will bring it right to the room, that is great!' Louis responds promptly in their talk, refusing to let the moment slip past.
Запомни, у нас двести второй номер.
'Remember, we have room two hundred and two.' Louis sharpens one classic term with Kostya: "vtoroy" means "second", and it carries the main weight of what Louis is saying.
Большое спасибо тебе за помощь, Костя.

'Thank you very much for your help, Kostya.' Louis aims the remark without fuss: the everyday word "spasibo" ("thank you") grew out of an old blessing meaning "save you", and it anchors the whole line here.
Саша, присмотри пока за моим баром.
'Sasha, watch my bar for now.' Kostya pushes back pointedly as things stand, refusing to let the moment slip past.
Только смотри не делай как Луи!
'Just mind you do not do like Louis!' Kostya anchors one direct piece toward Senya: "smotri" means "look" (from "smotret"), giving the line its exact edge.
Скажи, тебе было сегодня очень вкусно?

'Tell us, was it very tasty for you today?' Senya voices that point with warmth: Russian keeps the exact word order of a normal statement here, turning it into a question for Kostya purely through rising pitch at the end.
Молодцы, вы честно заслужили свою награду.
'Well done, you honestly earned your reward.' Senya steps in honestly on the spot, testing Louis's reaction in the middle of the exchange.
Ну давай уже скорее награждай нас!
'Well come on and reward us quickly already!' Senya reaches for this telling choice at once: "nagrazhday" means "reward" (from "nagrazhdat"), giving the line its exact edge.
Мы честно кормили тебя два дня.
'We honestly fed you for two days.' Senya grounds one telling term right here: "chestno" means "honestly", and it carries the main weight of what Senya is saying.
Хорошо, ребята, закройте пока свои глаза.
'Alright, guys, close your eyes for now.' Louis fires back pointedly with Kostya, letting the remark speak for itself.
Мы уже закрыли глаза и ждём.
'We have already closed our eyes and are waiting.' Senya reaches for this vivid touch toward Louis: "zakryli" means "to close, to shut" (from "zakryt"), giving the line its exact edge.
Давай я сам принесу вам шампанское.
Принесёшь прямо в номер, это отлично!
Запомни, у нас двести второй номер.

Хорошо, ребята, закройте пока свои глаза.

Senya and Fedya grin with anticipation, completely unaware of the trick the model is about to play on them. See you next time!
